---
title: "Hungarian Reel Analyzer (untried)"
---

A pipeline for turning a Hungarian Instagram Reel into a language-learning breakdown: line-by-line translation plus a vocabulary list, driven by three local Ollama models.

**Status:** never actually run end-to-end — `instaloader` (the Instagram downloader it depends on) broke not long after this was written, before it could be tested. Parked here in case it's worth reviving with a different downloader.

## Pipeline

```bash
OLLAMA_HOST=http://your-server:11434 ./setup-models.sh   # one-time: creates hu-ear, hu-eye, hu-brain
OLLAMA_HOST=http://your-server:11434 python3 pipeline.py <instagram_reel_url>
```

1. **Download** — `instaloader` fetches the Reel's video.
2. **Extract** — `ffmpeg` pulls a 16kHz mono WAV and one JPEG frame per second.
3. **Transcribe** (`hu-ear`) — Hungarian audio → raw transcription.
4. **OCR** (`hu-eye`) — on-screen text/subtitles across up to 30 frames → deduplicated text list.
5. **Coordinate** (`hu-brain`) — transcript + OCR text → Markdown output: line-by-line Hungarian/English translation, then a vocabulary section (inflected forms cross-referenced to lemmas, grammatical notes, common function words excluded unless used non-obviously).

## Models

All three are [`gemma4`](https://ollama.com)-based Ollama models, defined by Modelfile with a fixed system prompt and low temperature for the extraction steps:

| Model | Base | Role |
|---|---|---|
| [`hu-ear`](modelfiles/Modelfile.ear) | `gemma4:e4b` | Hungarian ASR — raw transcription only |
| [`hu-eye`](modelfiles/Modelfile.eye) | `gemma4:e4b` | OCR across video frames |
| [`hu-brain`](modelfiles/Modelfile.brain) | `gemma4:32b` | Translation + vocabulary breakdown, fixed Markdown output format |

`setup-models.sh` creates all three on the target Ollama server via `ollama create`.

## Files

- [`pipeline.py`](pipeline.py) — the end-to-end driver
- [`setup-models.sh`](setup-models.sh) — one-time model setup
- `modelfiles/` — the three Ollama Modelfiles above

**Dependencies:** `ollama` (Python client), `instaloader`, `ffmpeg`.
